markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

Three observations motivate the experiment. First, Electronics has 15.53% sampled training-pair errors, versus below 0.35% for Movies_and_TV and CDs_and_Vinyl; these are training diagnostics, not validation results. Second, sampled causal and compatibility-view checks pass, but independently exported predictor parity remains unverified. Third, historical pooling cannot explicitly require a candidate to match recurring evidence. Candidate-conditioned scoring addresses this gap, while potentially favoring redundant products over useful complements.

Three research insights qualify this direction. FISM/Fossil establish candidate–history aggregation and positional weighting; NAIS/FBSM establish target-dependent weighting and content similarity [4–7]. Novelty therefore rests narrowly on the constrained corroboration operator. Recency research [1] cautions against assuming stronger decay improves accuracy; retain a fixed initial timescale. Sampled-metric research [2] distinguishes benchmark selection from full-catalog behavior; fusion research [8] additionally motivates checking component scales without candidate-set-dependent normalization.

These insights suggest three directions: candidate-specific evidence, temporal/score calibration, and diagnostic correctness.

## Framework and alternatives

| Method | Evidence destination | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Learned sequence representation | No explicit corroboration requirement |
| Starting residual | Historical ID-embedding pool | Candidate relevance remains indirect |
| FISM/NAIS/FBSM | Candidate–history aggregation | No explicit two-witness requirement |
| Proposed residual | Individual candidate score | Lexical agreement misses complements |

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each row gives positive and negative assessments for all three dimensions.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate-specific two-witness score [3–7] | 3/6/6 | Precise operator; interpretable evidence test; one learned gate | Strong precedent; lexical shortcuts; expensive exact scoring/export |
| Two fixed recency scales [1,5] | 3/6/4 | Simple combination; temporal flexibility; cheap arithmetic | Established approach; uncertain transfer; extra tuning/parity work |
| Duplicate-text witness grouping [3,7] | 4/6/6 | Explicit evidence units; reduces duplicates; deterministic preprocessing | Novelty unverified; may merge valid variants; threshold/control burden |

## Selected experiment

At 20% progress, retain **candidate-specific two-witness scoring**, with scale calibration and stronger controls. Fit frozen category-specific TF–IDF on unique training-history items’ titles/descriptions. For candidate i and causal prefix t, set a[j]=cosine(i,item[j]) exp(−age[j]/20). Define q(i,t)=max min(a[j],a[k]) over witnesses with distinct IDs, both different from i, separated by at least three retained events. Missing evidence gives zero.

Use s=s_SASRec+σ tanh(alpha)q, alpha initially zero. Freeze σ from baseline training-prefix logit dispersion; never normalize over evaluation candidates. This preserves weak evidence but does not guarantee adequate influence near rank ten. Diagnose score spreads and rank-boundary gaps only where host outputs permit.

Compare unchanged SASRec, corroboration, matched maximum-similarity fusion, and shuffled-text corroboration with equal allowances. Other pooling rules remain budgeted follow-ups. Verify brute-force support, prefix causality and exported scores across all routes. Preserve diagnosis interfaces, seeds, splits and routing; select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10 within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Twenty-user full-catalog inspection remains descriptive; compatibility, ownership and unmet needs remain unknown without explicit evidence.

References: [1] arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [2] research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [3] github.com/devUuung/TRACE; [4] chbrown.github.io/kdd-2013-usb/kdd/p659.pdf; [5] arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152; [6] arxiv.org/abs/1809.07053; [7] arxiv.org/abs/1904.11799; [8] aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.290/

idea.description: Replace the history-pooling residual with a candidate-specific lexical corroboration score. Each candidate receives support only from two different historical item identities, separated by at least three retained events and different from the candidate. Add this bounded support through one zero-initialized scalar gate, multiplied by a frozen training-derived score scale, to the unchanged SASRec score.
idea.motivation: The previous branch corroborates historical anchors without explicitly corroborating each candidate. Candidate-conditioned scoring tests this gap using available titles, descriptions and histories. FISM, Fossil, NAIS and FBSM substantially precede candidate–history aggregation, temporal weighting and content similarity; the contribution is a narrowly defined evidence operator and its controlled evaluation. Electronics has weak sampled training-pair separation, but no supplied validation results establish that lexical corroboration will help. Lexical overlap can favor redundant alternatives and miss compatible complements. It cannot establish ownership, replacement intent, unmet need or factual compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, original splits, all four dataset routes, single-GPU execution and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Retain the baseline objective, optimizer, embeddings, positional indexing, sampler and training allowance for the first comparison. Store all artifacts beneath the trial directory. No experiments, filesystem inspection or training were performed for this proposal. The baseline training source and host predictor signature are not supplied, so this remains a specified research intervention rather than an executable replacement train.py.

Fit one sklearn TfidfVectorizer per dataset on unique training-history items in ascending item-ID order. Concatenate title, newline and description; absent fields become empty strings. Fix lowercase=True, analyzer='word', token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b', ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=2, max_df=1.0, max_features=20000, sublinear_tf=True, use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, norm='l2', stop_words=None and dtype=float64. Record the library version and serialize vocabulary, IDF, configuration, item mapping and CSR item matrix. Freeze the transform before processing other public item text. Missing text maps to zero, and an empty vocabulary disables the branch. Ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits in generic examples are unavailable and must not enter this experiment.

For a candidate i and retained causal prefix ending at t, assign each valid event its rank among retained events. Define a[j]=cosine(text[i],text[item[j]])*exp(-(rank[t]-rank[j])/20). Eligible witnesses j<k<=t require rank[k]-rank[j]>=3, item[j]!=item[k], item[j]!=i and item[k]!=i. q(i,t) is the maximum eligible min(a[j],a[k]), or zero. Thus q lies in [0,1]; confidence means deterministic lexical corroboration, not calibrated probability. Repetitions retain their chronological occurrences for spacing and decay, but two occurrences of one item cannot form the witness pair. Do not deduplicate chronological events before the spacing calculation. Recompute from the baseline's retained window; expired events must not remain witnesses. The timescale twenty and spacing three are fixed hypotheses, not established behavioral constants.

Return baseline_score(i,t)+sigma*tanh(alpha)*q(i,t), with one alpha per dataset initialized to zero. This replaces the earlier pooling branch; combining them is a separate experimental factor. Negative gates are permitted and their signs must be reported. At initialization, scores equal baseline scores exactly; the gate receives gradients when q is nonzero. The support statistic is fixed and nondifferentiable, while the original SASRec parameters still receive baseline-loss gradients. Bound the contribution by sigma without normalizing weak q upward. A bounded addition of one raw logit unit can be ineffective or excessive depending on rank-boundary gaps, so the original difficulty and potential ratings were too optimistic.

Define sigma reproducibly using the unchanged baseline's selected checkpoint, with checkpoint selection performed only through the permitted host validation objective. For each dataset, enumerate training prediction prefixes with at least one observed context event and an observed next training event, using stable user-ID and chronological ordering. Select up to 256 distinct prefix indices uniformly without replacement using a local NumPy default_rng(42), recording the selected indices and RNG algorithm. Use a separate local default_rng(42) to select up to 100 distinct nonpadding training-history item IDs, from sorted IDs, as one fixed reference candidate set. These candidates need not be unseen: this is a score-dispersion probe, not an accuracy estimate. Score every selected prefix against that reference set in evaluation mode. Subtract each prefix's mean reference logit, then set sigma=max(sqrt(mean(centered_logits**2)),1e-3), calculated in float64. Freeze and serialize sigma and reference records; if fewer than two reference items exist, use sigma=1 and mark the estimate unavailable. Nonfinite reference scores require investigation rather than silent replacement. Preserve global RNG states during this probe. The selected baseline checkpoint and this scale are shared by all residual controls. Residual arms start from the same seeded baseline initialization and receive equal training allowances; do not give one arm an extra fine-tuning stage.

This reference scale avoids candidate-set-dependent normalization and aligns score units only approximately. Residual-arm SASRec logits can drift away from the baseline scale during joint training; report their dispersion and learned gate rather than assuming calibration. Where the host exposes validation candidate scores, inspect baseline/content spreads, zero-support rates, and gaps between ranks ten and eleven without requesting additional labels or changing evaluation. If these outputs are unavailable, omit this diagnostic. A small prespecified fusion-weight grid including zero is a later alternative to joint gate learning, with all tuning charged to the budget. Do not combine a fusion grid, temporal search and architectural search by default. Min–max normalization, z-score normalization and reciprocal rank fusion are alternatives, not guaranteed improvements; normalization over the current candidate set can alter sampled-versus-catalog behavior and is excluded from this first experiment.

L2-normalized CSR rows give exact cosine through candidate-row times history-row transpose. Deduplicate IDs only for computing similarities, then map scores back to chronological occurrences. Bound both candidate and history blocks and immediately reduce each block; sparse products may become dense. Avoid catalog-by-catalog matrices. Cache or precompute deterministic support for fixed training windows only when storage and preprocessing are accounted for, and retain exact support for the supplied positive and negative IDs. Do not silently replace the baseline negative sampler. The reference pseudocode uses pair enumeration; it is a correctness oracle, not the intended large-scale training implementation.

For an exact O(L) reduction per candidate-prefix query after similarities are available, fix t and form the decayed a[j]. Scan the right witness k chronologically. Before querying k, insert position k-3 into a structure holding the two highest per-item-ID maxima among eligible left witnesses; exclude the candidate ID before insertion. Query the largest retained maximum whose ID differs from item[k], skipping a right witness equal to the candidate. Update best=max(best,min(a[k],eligible_max)). Two distinct-label maxima suffice for this single exclusion because no event expires within this fixed-prefix scan. Resolve ties by ascending item ID and earliest occurrence. Update an existing retained label with its maximum; discarded labels can reenter when a later occurrence exceeds the retained threshold. Zero scores may remain represented, although missing eligible witnesses and zero-valued witnesses both yield q=0 here.

For computing every training prefix, either repeat the fixed-prefix scan or implement a separately verified incremental version. In the latter, advance by uniformly decaying retained left maxima and the running pair optimum, insert the newly spacing-eligible left occurrence at its current decayed value, and query the current right witness. Uniform decay preserves ordering while the retained window is fixed. Truncated/sliding windows require rebuilding or expiration-aware per-label structures; two global maxima alone cannot recover replacements after expiration. Sparse similarity construction, prefix handling and full-catalog inference can dominate runtime despite the small parameter count. Profile before reserving training allocations, and count profiling and failures against the shared budget.

Prespecify four primary arms: unchanged SASRec; the candidate-specific two-witness branch; a matched maximum-similarity branch q_max=max_j a[j] with historical IDs different from the candidate; and two-witness scoring with whole-text reassignment. Both content rules share TF–IDF representations, scale, decay, gate initialization, optimizer, checkpoint cadence and training allowance. Maximum pooling tests whether requiring two witnesses helps beyond one-match retrieval. Do not claim it isolates spacing separately. Normalized sum, recency-weighted sum, distinct-ID top-two mean, unconstrained second-largest similarity, no-decay scoring, strongest-witness removal and duplicate-grouping are optional separately budgeted controls. Without spacing, maximum pairwise minimum equals the second-largest per-ID maximum; with spacing, sorting two per-ID scores alone is insufficient.

For the shuffled-text arm, use seed 0 to permute whole title/description documents within each dataset and joint strata of training-frequency decile, whitespace-token-count decile and text availability. Assign deciles from training-history items with stable item-ID tie breaking; leave singleton strata unchanged. Refit the identical TF–IDF specification on reassigned training documents. Nontraining items retain their public text and are transformed with that arm's frozen transform. Serialize the permutation and report the fraction actually reassigned. Coarse matching and singleton strata limit this control. Word-order shuffling does not adequately destroy unigram overlap.

Record exact baseline settings, arm order, checkpoint cadence, selection rules, runtime estimates and GPU-second allocations before execution. Count baseline training, scale estimation, profiling, failures, diagnosis, tuning and evaluation against the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Do not assume four equal-allowance arms fit before profiling or shorten controls after seeing their scores. If they do not fit, state which comparisons remain incomplete. Each arm retains all four categories. Select configurations solely by host-computed unweighted macro validation HR@10 using 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Use the same prespecified checkpoint opportunities for each arm and report per-category scores and the macro mean. These are sampled-candidate outcomes; training margins and full-catalog inspection answer different questions. Never access hidden test labels or files, fetch external data or pretrained weights, or alter the host evaluator.

If paired validation hits are exposed by the host, retain aligned records and use 10,000 seed-42 within-category bootstrap resamples for paired macro differences. Otherwise omit intervals. Such intervals condition on trained checkpoints and candidate sets and exclude training-seed variability and adaptive-selection bias. With only 800 validation users, extra weight, timescale, spacing and checkpoint searches increase selection risk. Prespecify descriptive history-length, target-frequency and text-availability strata without subgroup tuning. Do not infer generalization from the unusually large training margins in Movies_and_TV or CDs_and_Vinyl.

Shortcut risks include shared brands, boilerplate, generic descriptions, duplicated text across distinct IDs and correlations between text overlap and item popularity. Distinct IDs do not establish independent semantic evidence. Report training-only duplicate-text rates, support coverage and the fraction of maxima attributable to repeated IDs or exact duplicate descriptions. Missing or sparse metadata can make the operator mostly inactive; short prefixes cannot satisfy the spacing rule. True emerging interests and useful complements may have little lexical corroboration. Strongest-witness removal with count- and position-matched random controls can probe dependence, but perturbation effects do not establish causal user preferences. Keep the original candidate/exclusion set fixed when masking history so deleted items do not become newly eligible.

Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py restores the trained SASRec architecture, frozen text transform, item mapping, sigma, gate and identical candidate support. Ensure the host candidate-scoring path uses the same retained window, padding, positional convention and final valid-position selection as training. Full-catalog recommendations must separately exclude padding and previously seen items, without changing the host benchmark's candidate protocol. Score catalog chunks and immediately reduce support; compare chunk sizes to verify score invariance. Twenty real training users, five per category, receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for descriptive simulator inspection. They do not establish population preferences. Compatibility judgments require explicit requirement/specification evidence; absent evidence remains unknown, and histories alone establish neither ownership nor satisfaction.

Verify the optimized reducer against brute-force pair enumeration, unchanged scores at alpha=0, prefix invariance under position-preserving future masking, and training-side/exported score parity with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 in float32 scoring. Cover every dataset route, missing text, empty vocabulary, repeated IDs, tied similarities, insufficient witnesses, candidate-ID exclusions, all-padding sequences, one-event prefixes, truncated windows and different candidate chunks. Score parity must be supplemented by ranking agreement on identical candidate sets with consistent tie handling. Compare serialized-and-reloaded predictor results directly; compatibility-view parity does not establish export parity.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module, and item_emb must expose the trained embedding table. Because candidate scoring requires history, the original B x L x D feature tensor alone is insufficient. Adapt the view and probes together using an explicit feature carrier containing base_features shaped B x L x D and exact integer context_ids shaped B x L. predict_score must score each supplied B x L item against only its corresponding causal prefix; final-candidate scoring must explicitly select the final valid prefix. Compare learned coordinates and integer IDs separately in causal/parity probes. This is an explicit extension of the original feature-return contract and requires updating all consumers, including the predictor writer; if a host consumer requires tensor-only features, integrate an architecture-compatible representation there before running trials. Avoid mutable last-sequence caches and floating-point packing of IDs. user_train, meta_data and review_data retain their interfaces, with unavailable fields unavailable. Restore module modes and Python, NumPy, Torch and initialized CUDA RNG states after probes. Keep embedding alignment and training margins descriptive, and mark unsupported observations unavailable rather than reporting successful zeros.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
# Preserve baseline splits, routing, preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42.
# Record arm allocations and selection/checkpoint rules before execution.
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    text = fit_and_freeze_specified_tfidf(unique_training_history_items(dataset))
    baseline_checkpoint = run_budgeted_unchanged_baseline(dataset)
    sigma = frozen_training_reference_logit_scale(baseline_checkpoint)
    model = baseline_sasrec_with_original_seeded_initialization(dataset)
    alpha = Parameter(0.0)

    def candidate_support(prefix, candidate):
        events = retained_valid_events(prefix)
        a = [cosine(text[candidate], text[event])
             * exp(-(len(events) - 1 - j) / 20.0)
             for j, event in enumerate(events)]
        best = 0.0
        for j in range(len(events)):
            for k in range(j + 3, len(events)):
                if len({candidate, events[j], events[k]}) == 3:
                    best = max(best, min(a[j], a[k]))
        return best

    # Exact optimized fixed-prefix reducer:
    # scan k; insert eligible k-3 into top-two distinct-label maxima;
    # exclude candidate label and right-witness label before reduction.
    # Verify against the pair-enumeration definition above.

    for sequence, positive, negative in baseline_training_batches:
        base_features = model.log2feats(sequence)
        for valid supervised position t and batch row b:
            prefix = sequence[b, :t + 1]
            pos_score[b,t] = baseline_score(base_features[b,t], positive[b,t])
            neg_score[b,t] = baseline_score(base_features[b,t], negative[b,t])
            pos_score[b,t] += sigma * tanh(alpha) * candidate_support(prefix, positive[b,t])
            neg_score[b,t] += sigma * tanh(alpha) * candidate_support(prefix, negative[b,t])
        optimize_unchanged_baseline_loss_on_valid_positions()

    serialize_model_text_scale_gate_and_configuration_under_trial_directory()
    update_predictor_writer_with_identical_candidate_scoring()
    verify_bruteforce_causality_reload_score_and_ranking_parity()
    verify_updated_diagnostic_feature_carrier_and_scoring_contract()

# Run matched maximum-similarity and shuffled-text arms only within recorded budget.
# Retain all four categories in each arm; select using host macro validation HR@10.
# Report attempted configurations, accounted GPU seconds and incomplete controls.

originality.positive: The explicit distinct-ID, distance-constrained max–min operator provides a precise, falsifiable candidate-level corroboration rule.
originality.negative: FISM, Fossil, NAIS and FBSM closely precede candidate–history scoring, temporal weighting and content similarity. Without spacing, the operator reduces to a second-largest distinct-ID similarity; exact-rule novelty remains unverified.

future_potential.positive: Matched one-witness and shuffled-text controls could clarify whether repeated candidate-specific evidence contributes beyond sequential modeling and simple lexical retrieval.
future_potential.negative: Lexical shortcuts, sparse metadata and preference emergence may limit transfer. The mechanism can reinforce redundant alternatives and cannot resolve compatibility or unmet needs from the available observations.

code_difficulty.positive: The trainable change is one scalar per dataset, and both its mathematical definition and an exact fixed-prefix reducer are independently checkable.
code_difficulty.negative: Sparse candidate-conditioned scoring across training prefixes and full catalogs, frozen scale estimation, expiration handling, feature-contract changes and exported predictor parity create substantial integration and runtime costs.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary describes a recency metric and accuracy costs from excessive recent-item emphasis in evaluated models.
Motivates treating positional decay as an experimental hypothesis.
limitations: Does not establish an appropriate timescale for these four datasets.
Does not validate candidate-specific two-witness scoring.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons, including in expectation.
Supports distinguishing pinned sampled-candidate HR@10 from full-catalog inspection.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host evaluator.
Does not identify which intervention will improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: TRACE
contributions: The supplied summary describes influence-guided history edits assessed through ranking margins.
Motivates controlled witness-removal and history-dependence probes.
limitations: Perturbation sensitivity does not establish causal user preferences.
Does not establish the effectiveness of lexical corroboration.

related_work.title: FISM: Factored Item Similarity Models for Top-N Recommender Systems
contributions: Direct precedent for candidate-to-history scoring through learned item similarities.
Uses history-length normalization in additive aggregation.
limitations: Uses collaborative similarities rather than the proposed fixed lexical features.
Does not explicitly require two distinct corroborating witnesses.

related_work.title: Fossil: Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines item-similarity modeling with weighted recent interactions.
Provides precedent for positional weighting with global and user-specific components.
limitations: Sequence-lag weighting is not elapsed-time decay.
Does not establish the proposed constrained max–min rule.

related_work.title: NAIS: Neural Attentive Item Similarity Model for Recommendation
contributions: Learns candidate-dependent attention over historical items.
Provides a close precedent for target-conditioned history aggregation.
limitations: Learned attention does not explicitly enforce two distinct witnesses.
Does not establish that fixed lexical corroboration improves SASRec.

related_work.title: Feature-Based Similarity Models for Recommendation
contributions: Learns bilinear content similarities between candidate features and historically preferred items.
Connects item-feature interactions to candidate–history recommendation.
limitations: Feature interactions do not themselves establish corroboration by distinct historical items.
Does not support compatibility, ownership or unmet-need conclusions.

related_work.title: Hybrid fusion research supplied in the reflection results
contributions: Discusses normalized score fusion and rank fusion.
Motivates checking component scales and comparing fusion rules under matched tuning allowances.
limitations: Normalization does not establish calibrated relevance probabilities.
Does not validate the proposed frozen training-reference scale or this benchmark intervention.

related_work.title: Elasticsearch linear retriever documentation
contributions: Documents normalized weighted sums as an implemented hybrid retrieval mechanism.
limitations: Implementation precedent is not evidence of recommendation accuracy.
Candidate-population-dependent normalization requires care when transferring between sampled candidates and full catalogs.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn cosine similarity documentation
contributions: Documents cosine similarity and sparse output for sparse inputs.
Supports exact candidate–history similarity computation from normalized item rows.
limitations: Sparse output can still contain many nonzero entries.
Does not implement the proposed witness constraints or temporal reduction.

related_work.title: SciPy CSR matrix documentation
contributions: Documents compressed sparse row storage and row-oriented operations used for item-text lookup.
limitations: Does not guarantee that candidate–history products remain sparse or inexpensive.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn chunked pairwise distance documentation
contributions: Documents chunked pairwise computation with immediate reduction.
Provides an implementation pattern for bounded-memory catalog scoring.
limitations: An explicit CSR product with application-specific blocking may be more suitable here.
Chunking controls memory but does not remove total computation costs.
